Hallmark holds a hard floor and then gets out of the way. It deals three themes from a catalog of forty-eight materials, builds the page around what the visitor came to do, and lints the result in a real browser against the tells that read as machine-made: the eyebrow above every heading, tracked-capital labels, one coloured word in a headline, a page of empty frames or nothing but photographs, a hero that misses its screen, an email sign-up at the end of every page, a form that says thanks without sending anything. candidates.readme_excerpt: # Beautiful Rust A standard [Agent Skill](https://agentskills.io), `rust-best-practices`, that teaches coding agents to write idiomatic, robust, maintainable Rust. It works with Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and any other agent that reads the Agent Skills format. Once installed, it loads whenever a task involves Rust, cargo, crates, the borrow checker, clippy, or `.rs` files. The guidance is distilled from five sources, with a condensed digest of each bundled in the skill so the agent can consult the original reasoning when it needs to: - [Google Rust Style Guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/rustguide.html) - [Rust API Guidelines](https://rust-lang.github.io/api-guidelines/) (official rust-lang checklist) - [Effective Rust](https://www.lurklurk.org/effective-rust/) by David Drysdale - [Rust Design Patterns](https://rust-unofficial.github.io/patterns/) (idioms, patterns, anti-patterns) - [Microsoft Pragmatic Rust Guidelines](https://microsoft.github.io/rust-guidelines/) Where the sources disagree, the skill picks a side and says why. ## What it changes Asked for a small semver-parsing library, an agent without the skill produced working code with public fields, no `# Errors` docs, and `unwrap()` in its doc examples. With the skill, the same agent kept the fields private, documented failure modes, and wrote doc examples users can copy safely. Condensed from those two runs: ```rust // Without the skill /// A semantic version. candidates.description: Specification and documentation for Agent Skills
candidates.readme_excerpt:
# Agent Skills

[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/MKPE9g8aUy)

A standardized way to give AI agents new capabilities and expertise.

## What are Agent Skills?

Agent Skills are a lightweight, open format for extending AI agent capabilities with specialized knowledge and workflows.

At its core, a skill is a folder containing a `SKILL.md` file. This file includes metadata (`name` and `description`, at minimum) and instructions that tell an agent how to perform a specific task. Skills can also bundle scripts, reference materials, templates, and other resources.

```
my-skill/
├── SKILL.md          # Required: metadata + instructions
├── scripts/          # Optional: executable code
├── references/       # Optional: documentation
├── assets/           # Optional: templates, resources
└── ...               # Any additional files or directories
```

## Why Agent Skills?

Agents are increasingly capable, but often don't have the context they need to do real work reliably. Skills solve this by packaging procedural knowledge and company-, team-, and user-specific context into portable, version-controlled folders that agents load on demand. This gives agents:

- **Domain expertise**: Capture specialized knowledge — from legal review processes to data analysis pipelines to presentation formatting — as reusable instructions and resources.
- **Repeatable workflows**: Turn multi-step tasks into consistent, auditable procedures.
- **Cross-product reuse**: Build a skill once and use it across any skills-compatible agent.

## How do Agent Skills work?

Agents load skills through **progressive disclosure**, in three stages:

1. **Discovery**: At startup, agents load only the name and description of each available skill, just enough to know when it might be relevant.

2. **Activation**: When a task matches a skill's description, the agent reads the full `SKILL.md` instructions into context.

3. **Execution**: The agent follows the instructions, optionally executing bundled code or loading referenced files as needed.

Full instructions load only when a task calls for them, so agents can keep many skills on hand with only a small context footprint.

## Where can I use Agent Skills?

Agent Skills are supported by a large number of AI tools and agentic clients — see the [Client Showcase](https://agentskills.io/clients) to explore some of them!

## Getting started

- **[Documentation](https://agentskill

# sam3-segmentation

[![Test](https://github.com/lillyguisnet/sam3-segmentation/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/lillyguisnet/sam3-segmentation/actions/workflows/test.yml)

> This was mostly written by Opus 5.5 and not thoroughly checked by a human. It works on my machine, but haven't tested it elsewhere.

**An agent skill that outlines objects in photos with Meta's SAM 3, run on your
own NVIDIA GPU, and keeps everything it produces checkable.**

![Six agents on the same corn photo: kernel outlines drawn without tools (left half of each panel) and with this skill (right half)](docs/six-models/panel.jpg)

*Same six agents on the same corn photo, without tools (left half) and with this
skill (right half). Counts are each run's full set; nobody has checked these
outlines ([details](#does-it-work), [data](docs/six-models/record.json)). Photo:
ImageNet validation image ILSVRC2012_val_00000408; copyright belongs to its
original photographer and it is not covered by this repository's licence. It
will be removed on request.*

Ask your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, OpenCode and about 75
others) to "outline every kernel", "cut out the dog" or "count the seeds", and
this skill gives it the model, the commands and the rules to do it properly:

- **Quick calls:** every instance of a phrase ("all the jars"), more objects like
  an example box, one object from a click or a box, or "segment everything".
- **A careful workflow** for many small objects or parts (kernels, seeds, cells,
  insects): overlapping close-up crops, every raw candidate saved, score checks,
  review sheets and flags, recorded and reversible review decisions, boundary
  refinement, PNG and COCO RLE exports, and a zoomable viewer.
- **Honest output:** masks are reported as model proposals, never as verified
  ground truth, with what is uncertain listed.

## Install

Pick one. Each installs the same skill folder.

```sh
# Any agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, ...). Needs Node.js 22+.
npx skills add lillyguisnet/sam3-segmentation        # add -g for every project

# Claude Code plugin, with updates (Claude Code 2.1.275 or later):
/plugin install sam3-segmentation --marketplace lillyguisnet/sam3-segmentation

# No Node.js: copy the folder yourself (--target claude, codex or pi)
git clone https://github.com/lillyguisnet/sam3-seg
